name: The Starry Night
fact: Van Gogh painted it in 1889 from the window of his room at an asylum in Saint-Rémy, France, adding a village from his imagination. The swirling sky is one of the most famous in art; the real painting hangs in New York's Museum of Modern Art.

name: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
fact: It's a Japanese woodblock print, so thousands of copies were printed from carved wooden blocks. Look closely: tiny Mount Fuji sits in the background, and three boats of rowers are being tossed by the giant wave.

name: Mona Lisa
fact: Leonardo painted her on a thin panel of poplar wood. In 1911 she was stolen from the Louvre in Paris and missing for two years - which made her even more famous. Today she lives behind bulletproof glass.

name: Girl with a Pearl Earring
fact: Nobody knows who the girl was: it's a 'tronie', a Dutch painting of an imaginary face rather than a portrait of a real person. It hangs in the Mauritshuis museum in The Hague.

name: Sunflowers
fact: Van Gogh painted a whole series of sunflowers in Arles to decorate the bedroom of his friend, the painter Paul Gauguin, who was coming to stay. He used new bright yellow paints that had only just been invented.

name: Water Lilies
fact: Monet built a pond with a little Japanese bridge in his garden at Giverny, France, and painted its water lilies about 250 times during the last 30 years of his life.

name: Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton
by: western North America, about 66 million years ago
fact: T. rex lived at the very end of the age of dinosaurs. The most complete skeleton ever found, nicknamed Sue, is about 12 metres long, and its biggest teeth - roots included - are about 30 centimetres long. Birds are the living relatives of dinosaurs!

name: Giant moa skeleton
by: New Zealand, extinct about 600 years ago
fact: The giant moa was a flightless bird from New Zealand that could reach about 3.6 metres tall with its neck stretched up, and it had no wings at all. People once thought moas were the kiwi's closest cousins, but DNA showed the kiwi's closest relatives are the extinct elephant birds of Madagascar.

name: Iron meteorite
by: a piece of space, found in Oregon in 1902
fact: The Willamette Meteorite is a lump of iron and nickel that fell from space. It weighs about 15.5 tonnes - the largest meteorite ever found in North America.

name: Ammonite fossil
by: ancient seas, 400 to 66 million years ago
fact: Ammonites were sea creatures with coiled shells, related to today's octopuses and squid. They died out at the same time as the dinosaurs, and the biggest had shells nearly 2 metres across.

name: The Rosetta Stone
fact: The same message is carved on it three times: in Egyptian hieroglyphs, in Demotic script and in Ancient Greek. Because people could still read the Greek, it helped Jean-François Champollion crack the code of hieroglyphs in 1822. The real stone is in the British Museum.

name: Egyptian mummy
fact: Ancient Egyptians preserved bodies so the person could live on in the afterlife. Making a mummy took about 70 days: the body was dried out with a special salt called natron, then wrapped in many layers of linen.

name: The Wright Flyer
fact: On 17 December 1903 near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew it for 12 seconds and 37 metres - the first powered, controlled airplane flight. Later that day Wilbur flew it for 59 seconds. Pino can't fly, but this thing could!

name: Bell's telephone
fact: Bell said he came up with the idea for the telephone at his family's home in Brantford, Ontario, in 1874. In August 1876 he made one of the first long-distance calls, between Brantford and Paris, Ontario - about 13 kilometres.

name: Moon rock
by: the Moon, brought back by Apollo astronauts
fact: Between 1969 and 1972, Apollo astronauts brought back 382 kilograms of rock and soil from the Moon. Scientists still study it today to learn how the Moon formed.

name: Saturn V rocket
fact: The Saturn V carried the Apollo astronauts to the Moon. It was 111 metres tall - about as tall as a 36-storey building. Its first-stage engines burned about 13 tonnes of fuel and oxygen every second.

name: Model of the solar system
fact: Eight planets circle our Sun. Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it, and Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a giant enough bathtub.

name: Apollo spacesuit
fact: With its life-support backpack, an Apollo spacesuit weighed about 90 kilograms on Earth. On the Moon, where gravity is only one-sixth as strong, it felt like about 15 kilograms.

name: Canadarm
by: built in Canada, first flew in 1981
fact: Canadarm was a 15-metre robot arm built in Canada for NASA's Space Shuttle. It first flew in November 1981 and was used to catch satellites and help build the International Space Station.
